Small teams, high ownership. One person doing what three people used to do, because AI handles the rest.

AI just removed the bottleneck. And the role went with it.

AI always needs a human behind it.

Someone to direct it. Someone to judge the output. Someone to take responsibility for the result.

That human is not disappearing. That human is becoming more valuable because now they carry the leverage of an entire team.

The question is whether you're building yourself to be that person.

So the move isn't to outrun AI.

The move is to position yourself where AI multiplies you.

Smaller team, more ownership, real output and irreplaceable judgment.

That's the only safe seat at the table now.
